docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
MatGraph is a Deep Learning toolkit for Materials Science. It provides three interfaces to the same underlying prediction engine:

Interface Best for CLI (matgraph) Quick predictions, scripting, automation Python SDK (MatGraphSDK) Jupyter Notebooks, ML pipelines, custom scripts GraphQL API Web applications, microservices, dashboards

All three interfaces share the same models (M3GNet, MEGNet, CGCNN, CHGNet), the same Materials Project data source, and the same SQLite cache. New here? Start with Installation — the --demo mode gives you a first successful command in under a minute, no API key required.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: MatGraph CLI is built with Typer and Rich for a clean terminal experience.

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text:
matgraph --version    # Show MatGraph and Python version
matgraph --help       # Show all available commands

docs.title: predict
docs.text:
Run the ML prediction pipeline on a material formula.

matgraph predict FORMULA [OPTIONS]

Arguments: | Argument | Required | Description | |---|---|---| | FORMULA | Yes | Chemical formula (e.g., LiFePO4, NaCl, SiO2) |

Options: | Option | Default | Description | |---|---|---| | --model | cgcnn | Model architecture: cgcnn, megnet, or m3gnet | | --min-gap | None | Minimum band gap filter (eV) | | --max-gap | None | Maximum band gap filter (eV) | | --crystal-system | None | Filter by crystal system (e.g., Cubic, Hexagonal) | | --save | None | Output file path for results | | --format | json | Output format: json or csv | | --cif | False | Export 3D crystal structures as .cif files |

Examples:

# Basic prediction with default CGCNN model
matgraph predict LiFePO4

# Use M3GNet for energy/forces/stresses
matgraph predict LiFePO4 --model m3gnet

# Filter by band gap range and crystal system
matgraph predict LiFePO4 --min-gap 1.5 --max-gap 4.0 --crystal-system Cubic

# Export results to CSV with CIF structures
matgraph predict LiFePO4 --save results.csv --format csv --cif

docs.title: substitute
docs.text:
Simulate elemental substitution and predict thermodynamic stability. Inspired by Google DeepMind's GNoME paper.

matgraph substitute FORMULA ELEMENT_OUT ELEMENT_IN

Arguments: | Argument | Description | |---|---| | FORMULA | Base material formula | | ELEMENT_OUT | Element to remove | | ELEMENT_IN | Element to insert |

Example:

matgraph substitute LiFePO4 Li Na
# Predicts whether NaFePO4 is thermodynamically stable compared to LiFePO4

docs.title: xrd
docs.text:
Simulate the X-Ray Diffraction pattern for a material.

matgraph xrd FORMULA

Example:

matgraph xrd LiFePO4
# Shows top diffraction peaks with 2-theta angles and intensities

docs.title: evaluate
docs.text:
Evaluate model accuracy by computing Mean Absolute Error (MAE) against Materials Project ground truth.

matgraph evaluate FORMULA [--model MODEL]

Example:

matgraph evaluate LiFePO4 --model megnet

docs.title: MatGraph vs raw pymatgen + MatGL
docs.text: MatGraph is a workflow layer on top of pymatgen, MatGL, and mp-api — not a replacement. If you already script those libraries, here is exactly what MatGraph saves you, task by task.

docs.title: 1. Formation energy for one formula
docs.text:
Raw stack — fetch, load weights, infer, all by hand:

from mp_api.client import MPRester
import matgl

with MPRester(API_KEY) as mpr:
    docs = mpr.materials.summary.search(
        formula="LiFePO4",
        fields=["material_id", "structure", "formation_energy_per_atom"],
    )
model = matgl.load_model("M3GNet-Eform-MP-2019.4.1")  # downloads weights
for doc in docs:
    if doc.structure is None:
        continue
    eform = float(model.predict_structure(doc.structure).detach().item())
    print(doc.material_id, eform)

MatGraph — one command, with cache + provenance + seed handling built in:

matgraph predict LiFePO4 --model m3gnet --seed 42

from matgraph import MatGraphSDK
sdk = MatGraphSDK()
sdk.predict("LiFePO4", model="m3gnet", seed=42)

docs.title: 2. Screen hypothetical substitutions
docs.text:
Raw stack — loop over polymorphs, mutate structures, run the PES:

from mp_api.client import MPRester
from matgl.ext.ase import M3GNetCalculator
from pymatgen.io.ase import AseAtomsAdaptor
import matgl

pes = matgl.load_model("M3GNet-PES-MatPES-PBE-2025.2")
with MPRester(API_KEY) as mpr:
    docs = mpr.materials.summary.search(formula="LiFePO4", fields=["structure"])
base = docs[0].structure
new = base.copy()
new.replace_species({"Li": "Na"})  # hope the site order cooperates
for label, s in [("base", base), ("hypo", new)]:
    atoms = AseAtomsAdaptor.get_atoms(s)
    atoms.calc = M3GNetCalculator(potential=pes)
    print(label, atoms.get_potential_energy())

MatGraph — validated, deterministic, tabulated:

matgraph substitute LiFePO4 Li Na --seed 42

sdk.substitute("LiFePO4", "Li", "Na", seed=42)

docs.title: 3. Battery cathode triage
docs.text:
Raw stack — parse the composition, look up the Faraday constant, decide on a voltage model, wire it to ML output yourself.

MatGraph:

matgraph battery LiFePO4            # exact capacity, keyless with [mp]
matgraph battery LiFePO4 --demo     # zero-config sample

sdk.battery("LiFePO4")
# {'theoretical_capacity_mah_g': 169.89, 'avg_voltage_V_proxy': ..., ...}

docs.title: 4. Serve predictions to an app
docs.text:
Raw stack — write a FastAPI service, auth, validation, and error handling from scratch.

MatGraph:

pip install "matgraph-cli[api]"
matgraph auth generate --user "my-app"
matgraph serve   # GraphQL + POST /v1/predict, hashed keys, validation

docs.title: What you get beyond fewer lines
docs.text: Concern Raw stack MatGraph Repeated queries Re-fetch + re-infer every time Content-hashed SQLite cache Reproducibility Your own bookkeeping provenance on every result (checkpoint, versions, seed, device) Determinism Manual seeding per lib One --seed threads through all libs Batch + export Custom loops predict_many, CSV/JSON/Parquet, --cif Experiment tracking Print statements W&B-compatible local tracking + registry Newcomer onboarding Key + torch + weights first --demo works in 60 seconds, no key

docs.title: When to stay raw
docs.text:
• You need a model MatGraph doesn't wrap — use the libraries directly.
  • You are developing a new potential — MatGraph consumes checkpoints, it doesn't train foundation models (its train fits small task heads).
  • You need per-atom control of the relaxation loop — use ASE + MatGL.

Rule of thumb: libraries for research into models, MatGraph for research with models.

docs.title: GraphQL API Reference
docs.text: MatGraph includes an async GraphQL API built on FastAPI and Strawberry for integrating predictions into web applications.

docs.title: Starting the Server
docs.text:
uvicorn matgraph.graphql_app:app --reload

The server starts at http://localhost:8000. The interactive GraphiQL playground is available at http://localhost:8000/graphql.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: All requests require an x-api-key header.

docs.title: Generate a Key
docs.text:
matgraph auth generate --user "my-app"
# Output: mg_S8jvhzo58p6XQE_fS0Oru1WqG2AJR6x5

docs.title: Master Key (Alternative)
docs.text:
Set a master key via environment variable:

export MATGRAPH_API_KEY="my_master_key"

docs.title: Query: predictMaterial
docs.text:
query {
  predictMaterial(
    formula: String!
    minGap: Float
    maxGap: Float
    crystalSystem: String
    model: String = "cgcnn"
    limit: Int = 10
  ): [MaterialPrediction!]!
}

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
type MaterialPrediction {
  materialId: ID!
  formula: String!
  crystalSystem: String!
  trueBandGap: Float
  predictedBandGap: Float!
  trueFormEnergy: Float
  predictedFormEnergy: Float!
  features: MaterialFeatures!
  metrics: ModelMetrics!
}

type MaterialFeatures {
  numElements: Int!
  meanAtomicMass: Float!
  volume: Float!
  density: Float!
}

type ModelMetrics {
  modelName: String!
  confidenceScore: Float!
}

docs.title: Basic Prediction
docs.text:
query {
  predictMaterial(formula: "LiFePO4") {
    materialId
    formula
    predictedBandGap
    predictedFormEnergy
  }
}

docs.title: With Filters
docs.text:
query {
  predictMaterial(formula: "NaCl", minGap: 1.0, limit: 3, model: "megnet") {
    materialId
    formula
    crystalSystem
    trueBandGap
    predictedBandGap
    features {
      density
      volume
    }
    metrics {
      modelName
      confidenceScore
    }
  }
}

docs.title: cURL Example
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/graphql \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "query": "query { predictMaterial(formula: \"LiFePO4\", model: \"megnet\") { formula predictedBandGap predictedFormEnergy } }"
  }'

docs.title: Python (requests)
docs.text:
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "http://localhost:8000/graphql",
    json={"query": '{ predictMaterial(formula: "LiFePO4") { formula predictedBandGap } }'},
    headers={"x-api-key": "YOUR_KEY"}
)
print(response.json())

docs.title: JavaScript (fetch)
docs.text:
const response = await fetch("http://localhost:8000/graphql", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "x-api-key": "YOUR_KEY",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    query: `{ predictMaterial(formula: "LiFePO4") { formula predictedBandGap } }`,
  }),
});
const data = await response.json();
console.log(data);

docs.title: Models
docs.text: MatGraph ships with three deep learning architectures for material property prediction.

docs.title: CGCNN (Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Network)
docs.text:
Paper: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties (Xie & Grossman, 2018)

Predicts: Band gap, Formation energy per atom

How it works: 1. Represents a crystal as a graph where nodes are atoms and edges are bonds 2. Applies graph convolutions to learn atom-level representations 3. Pools atom features into a crystal-level descriptor 4. Passes through fully connected layers for property prediction

Usage:

matgraph predict LiFePO4 --model cgcnn

results = sdk.predict("LiFePO4", model="cgcnn")

docs.title: MEGNet (MatErials Graph Network)
docs.text:
Paper: Graph Networks as a Universal Machine Learning Framework for Molecules and Crystals (Chen et al., 2019)

Predicts: Band gap, Formation energy per atom

How it works: 1. Encodes atoms, bonds, and global state as separate feature vectors 2. Updates all three through message-passing layers 3. Global state captures crystal-wide properties 4. Outputs property predictions from the global state vector

Key difference from CGCNN: MEGNet explicitly models global state information (total charge, composition features), which improves accuracy for properties that depend on the overall crystal rather than individual atoms.

Usage:

matgraph predict LiFePO4 --model megnet

results = sdk.predict("LiFePO4", model="megnet")

docs.title: M3GNet (Multi-body M3GNet)
docs.text:
Paper: A universal graph deep learning interatomic potential for the periodic table (Chen & Ong, 2022)

Predicts: Total energy, Atomic forces, Stress tensor

How it works: 1. Encodes atoms with embeddings based on atomic number 2. Computes 2-body interactions (pairwise distances) 3. Computes 3-body interactions (bond angles) 4. Multi-layer message passing with both 2-body and 3-body information 5. Predicts energy as the sum of atomic contributions 6. Forces and stresses are derived from energy gradients

Key difference from CGCNN/MEGNet: M3GNet is a universal interatomic potential. Instead of predicting a single property, it predicts the potential energy surface, from which forces and stresses can be computed. This makes it suitable for molecular dynamics and structure relaxation.

Usage:

matgraph predict LiFePO4 --model m3gnet

results = sdk.predict("LiFePO4", model="m3gnet")
print(f"Energy: {results[0]['m3gnet_energy']} eV")
print(f"Forces: {results[0]['m3gnet_forces']}")

docs.text: Property CGCNN MEGNet M3GNet Band gap Yes Yes No Formation energy Yes Yes No Total energy No No Yes Atomic forces No No Yes Stress tensor No No Yes Architecture GCN Graph Network Multi-body GNN Best for Property screening Property screening Stability analysis

docs.title: matgraph.nn — a PyTorch-native framework for materials
docs.text: Goal: the everyday materials-ML workflow (structure → graph → model → train → checkpoint) expressed as ordinary torch.nn.Module code, with no DGL or MatGL dependency and no simulated numbers.

docs.title: Phase 1 (implemented)
docs.text:
Piece File What it does Graph construction matgraph/nn/graph.py Periodic neighbor graph from lattice + fractional coords (numpy). Images searched far enough for any cell shape. max_neighbors nearest kept. Batching matgraph/nn/graph.py collate_crystals merges crystals with per-atom crystal ids and offset edges. CrystalDataset for DataLoader. Layers matgraph/nn/layers.py GaussianExpansion (distance basis), CGConv (gated crystal convolution, LayerNorm). Model matgraph/nn/models.py CrystalGNN: embedding → CGConv stack → mean pool → MLP. Config-driven, rebuildable. Trainer matgraph/nn/train.py fit (optional early stopping that restores best weights), evaluate, predict, save, load_checkpoint. Reports only metrics computed from the data passed in. Tests tests/test_nn.py 26 tests: periodic images (incl. non-orthogonal fcc), wrap invariance, batch offsets, batch independence, checkpoint round trip, loss decreasing on a learnable target.

Usage:

from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from matgraph.nn import build_crystal_graph, CrystalDataset, collate_crystals, CrystalGNN, Trainer

graphs = [build_crystal_graph(lat, frac, Z, cutoff=5.0, target=[e_form]) for lat, frac, Z, e_form in data]
loader = DataLoader(CrystalDataset(graphs), batch_size=32, shuffle=True, collate_fn=collate_crystals)
trainer = Trainer(CrystalGNN(num_targets=1), lr=1e-3)
trainer.fit(loader, epochs=50)
trainer.save("runs/eform.pt")

docs.title: Phase 2 (done)
docs.text: Item Status Where Fake finetune removed Done. simulate_finetune and the finetune-simulate CLI command are deleted. finetune trains for real, and the active-learning retrain loop calls it. Failures are logged, not swallowed. matgraph/training/finetune.py, matgraph/core.py Pymatgen adapter tests Done. pymatgen is installed via uv sync --extra dev. Tests cover from_pymatgen vs the plain-dict path and as_dict() JSONL. tests/test_nn_pipeline.py Data from repo sources Done. CSV (structure JSON or cif column), JSONL of MaterialRecords (pymatgen as_dict layout), and graphs_from_records. The active-learning dataset file loads directly. matgraph/nn/data.py MatGL pretrained bridge Not done, by design. MatGL's M3GNet/CHGNet/MEGNet are different architectures (DGL/PyG, three-body terms). Their weights cannot be mapped onto CrystalGNN. finetune rejects them with an explicit error. Transfer learning works from matgraph checkpoints only. A real bridge would mean implementing those architectures natively. matgraph/training/finetune.py::_make_base Device and performance Done on CPU. Neighbor search is now a per-center loop (memory O(N·S), not O(N²·S)). Measured: 64-atom cell 2 ms, 216 atoms 20 ms; a training step on 32 crystals of 10 atoms 9 ms. CUDA/MPS not measured (no GPU here). matgraph/nn/graph.py Uncertainty Done as deep ensembles: std across independently seeded members. MC-dropout is not implemented. MaterialRecord.uncertainty is not yet filled automatically. matgraph/nn/ensemble.py CLI Done. matgraph train, matgraph finetune (alias), matgraph nn predict (several -c checkpoints = ensemble std). matgraph/cli.py

docs.title: Design rules
docs.text:
• Everything is a torch.nn.Module or a plain function over tensors; no hidden global state.
  • No fabricated metrics. If a metric cannot be computed, the code raises.
  • Graph construction has no optional dependencies. Adapters import lazily.
  • Checkpoints store the architecture config, so load_checkpoint never needs the original code path.

docs.title: Python SDK Reference
docs.text: The MatGraphSDK class provides a clean Python interface for use in Jupyter Notebooks, scripts, and ML pipelines.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: from matgraph import MatGraphSDK

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
sdk = MatGraphSDK(api_key="your_key")

If api_key is not provided, it reads from the MP_API_KEY environment variable.

docs.title: sdk.predict()
docs.text:
Run the ML prediction pipeline on a material.

sdk.predict(
    formula: str,
    model: str = "cgcnn",
    min_gap: float = None,
    max_gap: float = None,
    crystal_system: str = None
) -> List[Dict]

Parameters: | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | formula | str | required | Chemical formula | | model | str | "cgcnn" | "cgcnn", "megnet", or "m3gnet" | | min_gap | float | None | Minimum band gap filter | | max_gap | float | None | Maximum band gap filter | | crystal_system | str | None | Crystal system filter |

Returns: List of dictionaries containing predictions and metadata.

Example:

results = sdk.predict("LiFePO4", model="m3gnet")
for r in results:
    print(f"{r['formula']}: {r['m3gnet_energy']} eV")

docs.title: sdk.substitute()
docs.text:
Simulate elemental substitution and predict stability.

sdk.substitute(
    formula: str,
    element_out: str,
    element_in: str
) -> Dict

Parameters: | Parameter | Type | Description | |---|---|---| | formula | str | Base material formula | | element_out | str | Element to remove | | element_in | str | Element to insert |

Returns: Dictionary with original, hypothetical, and is_more_stable keys.

Example:

result = sdk.substitute("LiFePO4", element_out="Li", element_in="Na")
if result["is_more_stable"]:
    print(f"{result['hypothetical']['formula']} is stable")

docs.title: sdk.xrd()
docs.text:
Simulate an X-Ray Diffraction pattern.

sdk.xrd(formula: str) -> Dict

Returns: Dictionary with two_theta, intensity, and hkls arrays.

Example:

xrd = sdk.xrd("LiFePO4")

# Plot with matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.plot(xrd["two_theta"], xrd["intensity"])
plt.xlabel("2-theta (degrees)")
plt.ylabel("Intensity")
plt.title("XRD Pattern - LiFePO4")
plt.show()

docs.title: sdk.evaluate()
docs.text:
Compute Mean Absolute Error against ground truth.

sdk.evaluate(formula: str, model: str = "cgcnn") -> Dict

Returns: Dictionary with band_gap_mae, formation_energy_mae, and samples_evaluated.

Example:

metrics = sdk.evaluate("LiFePO4", model="megnet")
print(f"Band gap MAE: {metrics['band_gap_mae']:.4f} eV")
print(f"Formation energy MAE: {metrics['formation_energy_mae']:.4f} eV/atom")
print(f"Samples: {metrics['samples_evaluated']}")

docs.title: Batch Prediction
docs.text:
formulas = ["LiFePO4", "NaCl", "SiO2", "TiO2", "GaN"]
for formula in formulas:
    results = sdk.predict(formula)
    for r in results:
        print(f"{r['formula']}: gap={r['predicted_band_gap']:.2f} eV")

docs.title: Screening Loop for New Materials
docs.text:
import itertools

bases = ["LiFePO4", "LiCoO2", "LiMnO2"]
substitutions = [("Li", "Na"), ("Li", "K"), ("Li", "Mg")]

for base, (out, inp) in itertools.product(bases, substitutions):
    try:
        result = sdk.substitute(base, element_out=out, element_in=inp)
        status = "STABLE" if result["is_more_stable"] else "unstable"
        print(f"{base} -> {result['hypothetical']['formula']}: {status}")
    except ValueError:
        pass

docs.title: Export to Pandas DataFrame
docs.text:
import pandas as pd

results = sdk.predict("LiFePO4")
df = pd.DataFrame([{
    "material_id": r["material_id"],
    "formula": r["formula"],
    "band_gap": r["predicted_band_gap"],
    "formation_energy": r["predicted_form_energy"],
    "density": r["features"]["density"],
} for r in results])

print(df)
df.to_csv("predictions.csv", index=False)

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text: Practical walkthroughs for common MatGraph workflows.

docs.title: Tutorial 0: First run in 60 seconds (no API key)
docs.text:
Every tutorial below uses live predictions, which need pip install "matgraph-cli[ml]" plus a free Materials Project key. But you can learn the whole interface first on bundled demo data — no key, no PyTorch:

pip install matgraph-cli
matgraph predict LiFePO4 --demo     # sample prediction
matgraph battery LiFePO4 --demo     # cathode screening (exact 169.89 mAh/g)
matgraph xrd Si --demo              # real Cu-Ka pattern

from matgraph import MatGraphSDK

Demo output is loudly labeled: structures, XRD, and capacity are real crystallography; ML numbers are illustrative samples. When you're ready for live predictions, continue to Installation.

docs.title: Tutorial 1: Screen Battery Cathode Materials
docs.text:
Find which alkali metal substitutions in LiFePO4 produce stable cathode candidates.

from matgraph import MatGraphSDK

sdk = MatGraphSDK()

base = "LiFePO4"
candidates = ["Na", "K", "Mg", "Ca", "Zn"]

print(f"Screening substitutions for {base}")
print("-" * 50)

for element in candidates:
    try:
        result = sdk.substitute(base, element_out="Li", element_in=element)
        new_formula = result["hypothetical"]["formula"]
        stable = "STABLE" if result["is_more_stable"] else "UNSTABLE"
        delta_e = result["hypothetical"]["energy"] - result["original"]["energy"]
        print(f"  {base} -> {new_formula}: {stable} (delta E = {delta_e:.4f} eV)")
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"  {element}: skipped ({e})")

docs.title: Tutorial 2: Compare Model Architectures
docs.text:
Evaluate all three models on the same material and compare accuracy.

from matgraph import MatGraphSDK

sdk = MatGraphSDK()

formula = "SiO2"
models = ["cgcnn", "megnet"]

print(f"Model comparison for {formula}")
print("-" * 40)

for model in models:
    metrics = sdk.evaluate(formula, model=model)
    print(f"  {model.upper()}")
    print(f"    Band gap MAE:    {metrics['band_gap_mae']:.4f} eV")
    print(f"    Form energy MAE: {metrics['formation_energy_mae']:.4f} eV/atom")
    print(f"    Samples:         {metrics['samples_evaluated']}")
    print()

docs.title: Tutorial 3: Build an XRD Database
docs.text:
Generate XRD patterns for a list of materials and save to a JSON file.

import json
from matgraph import MatGraphSDK

sdk = MatGraphSDK()

materials = ["LiFePO4", "NaCl", "TiO2", "SiO2", "GaN", "ZnO"]
xrd_database = {}

for formula in materials:
    try:
        xrd = sdk.xrd(formula)
        xrd_database[formula] = {
            "num_peaks": len(xrd["two_theta"]),
            "strongest_peak_angle": xrd["two_theta"][xrd["intensity"].index(max(xrd["intensity"]))],
            "pattern": xrd
        }
        print(f"  {formula}: {len(xrd['two_theta'])} peaks")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  {formula}: failed ({e})")

with open("xrd_database.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(xrd_database, f, indent=2)

print(f"\nSaved {len(xrd_database)} patterns to xrd_database.json")

docs.title: Tutorial 4: Export Predictions to Pandas
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
from matgraph import MatGraphSDK

sdk = MatGraphSDK()

formulas = ["LiFePO4", "NaCl", "SiO2", "TiO2", "GaN"]
rows = []

for formula in formulas:
    results = sdk.predict(formula)
    for r in results:
        rows.append({
            "material_id": r["material_id"],
            "formula": r["formula"],
            "crystal_system": r["crystal_system"],
            "band_gap_true": r["true_band_gap"],
            "band_gap_pred": r["predicted_band_gap"],
            "form_energy_true": r["true_form_energy"],
            "form_energy_pred": r["predicted_form_energy"],
            "density": r["features"]["density"],
            "volume": r["features"]["volume"],
        })

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(df.describe())
df.to_csv("matgraph_dataset.csv", index=False)

docs.title: Frontend (JavaScript)
docs.text:
async function predictMaterial(formula) {
  const response = await fetch("http://localhost:8000/graphql", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "x-api-key": "mg_your_key_here",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      query: `
        query($formula: String!) {
          predictMaterial(formula: $formula) {
            formula
            crystalSystem
            predictedBandGap
            predictedFormEnergy
            features { density volume }
          }
        }
      `,
      variables: { formula },
    }),
  });
  return response.json();
}

// Usage
predictMaterial("LiFePO4").then(data => console.log(data));
